decisions.reason: The rye country bread extends the firm's core traditional bread range, so its incremental investment is part of an established direction that management will keep defending.

The premium raisin stollen is the publicly announced flagship and has again won the gold medal of the Deutsches Brotinstitut, so both its visible commitment and its success argue strongly for keeping it.
The seeded rye mixed bread builds on the established rye range and has its own page, so management sees little reason to reverse its earlier decision.
The dark barley malt rye is a niche variant, but it shares the firm's existing know-how and facilities, and weaker demand can still be blamed on temporary causes.
The marzipan stollen complements the flagship stollen line in the seasonal gift business, so dropping it would undercut the firm's committed Christmas direction.
The firm publicly presented the ancient grain bread as its newest masterpiece, so having just announced it, management is committed to giving it time to prove itself.
